root_cause_assessment.hypothesis: SCM Stopped was visible before original service process released its executable image.
support: The repair waits for SCM Stopped only, then immediately copies executable.
The service code returns from handler to svc.Run before main returns; a status observation alone does not prove process termination.
A freshly created service PID was observed running the unchanged old binary shortly after the failed repair.
There are no other broker.exe processes in this after-failure snapshot.
limits: No failing-instant process list or stable old process handle was recorded.
A transient client process or other mapping holder at failure time cannot be excluded.
Post-failure current state cannot establish exact ordering inside the failure and catch path.

bounded_revision_review_advice: Acquire and retain the original service process handle before Stop-Service; validate service PID identity and wait for that exact process to exit with a finite timeout before copy.
Do not kill arbitrary broker processes; on continued sharing violation preserve state and report contemporaneous processes.
Allow existing backups only when both files exist and their bytes match the verified old installation and current manifest. Preserve ACLs and do not overwrite existing backups.
Keep private data and existing unknown credential untouched.
